findings.title: Published standings lag one completed game
findings.detail: The site serves data built at 2026-11-12T23:37Z. That snapshot has NYG at 5-2-1 (182 PF / 172 PA) and WAS at 2-5-1 (172 PF / 202 PA). The official division standings read on 2026-11-13 at 12:05Z show NYG 5-3-1 (203/196) and WAS 3-5-1 (196/223), after the Week 10 Thursday game finished 24-21 to Washington. Every other club matches exactly.
findings.settle: Re-run the collect workflow after the Thursday game settled, or add the gate in SG-01.

findings.title: Two leaderboards publish different results under the same rule names
findings.detail: The landing page ranks 12 rules scored with a -110 price assumption over 2005-2026. The research board scores 12 rules using observed prices over 2006-2026 and ranks different rules. The names overlap (S04, S07, S09, S10, S11, S12) but the numbers do not: the -110 board's top row is a 4.2% ROI, the priced board's S09 is -7.9%. A reader cannot tell which is the competition.
findings.settle: Apply SG-02 and publish one headline board.

findings.title: Several site generations are published from one repository
findings.detail: Root dashboard, pages/, docs/, verified-lab/, referee/, lab/, dashboard/, research/ and this room/ all render overlapping tables with independently generated numbers and timestamps. Each is internally consistent; the set is not.
findings.settle: Publish the authoritative mapping (SG-07) rather than deleting independent builds.

findings.title: Depth-chart page covers 3 of 31 captured clubs
findings.detail: The scrape holds 934 position rows for 31 clubs with per-club source URLs; the rendered page shows KC, GB and SF only (85 rows). The 32nd club, HOU, publishes its chart as an image rather than a table, so its depth order cannot be transcribed as text and is labelled rather than guessed.
findings.settle: Render the full scrape (SG-05) and label HOU as 'chart published as an image'.

findings.title: 'No game designation yet' and 'fit' render the same way
findings.detail: Only 9 of 296 injury rows carry a game designation. The availability table blends practice participation into a single 0-100 attrition index with documented weights, so a club that has not published a designation is indistinguishable from a healthy club at a glance.

findings.title: Market column cites a page that publishes no odds
findings.detail: The own-lines table links each market spread and total to the official nfl.com schedule page. That page publishes fixtures, kick-off times and results, not closing spreads; the numbers come from the hash-pinned nflverse schedules file.

findings.title: Two generators write index.html; the one that commits is not the one the pull-request check audits
findings.detail: `pipeline/gen_site.py` renders the evidence-first dashboard and the collect-data workflow commits its output to `index.html` and `pages/`. `tools/build.py` also writes `index.html`, from a different template and a different data layer; it runs in the 'Verify NFL1 site' pull-request job immediately before `tools/verify.py`. The consequence is narrower than a broken site but still real: the check that runs on every pull request audits a regenerated substitute rather than the page that is served, and any local or ad-hoc run of `tools/build.py` overwrites the front door in the working tree. Reproduced locally: running `tools/build.py` changes `index.html` by 345 insertions and 84 deletions; `git checkout -- index.html` restores it. The committed page on `main` is the correct one, because the bot commits only `pipeline/gen_site.py` output.

here.note: gen_site.py then git add index.html pages

findings.settle: Apply SG-12: build.py writes legacy-site.html; tools/verify.py reads the new name. Then the pull-request check audits the served page.

findings.title: Correlation sample size is not reproducible from the committed file
findings.detail: C1 publishes n=6,975 with r=0.4312. Every row in data/s9cb/games.csv that has both a spread and a result gives n=7,103 and r=0.4309. The value reproduces; the filter that removes 128 games is not stated.

findings.title: The 296-row injury scrape reconciles with today's official page
findings.detail: Every club readable to its last row on the official Week 10 report matches the committed scrape exactly: 24 of 24 clubs, 0 row-count differences, 276 rows in the capture plus 20 rows in the two clubs recorded as partial. LAC and BAL publish 'No Injuries Reported'; CHI, DEN, PHI and TB are on bye.
findings.settle: Nothing - recorded as a passing check.

findings.title: Best priced strategy reproduces exactly from committed data
findings.detail: S07 'Fade the road favourite of 7+' recomputed independently from data/s9cb/games.csv using only rows that carry an observed price: 401 bets, 394 decided, 219 wins, 55.58% hit rate, +24.318 units, 6.064% ROI. Identical to the published row.
findings.settle: Nothing - recorded as a passing check.

findings.title: A club's published chart omits players the official injury report lists for that club
findings.detail: Kerby Joseph (S, #31) has an official Detroit Lions player page and appears in the club's roster navigation, but the club's depth chart lists only Chuck Clark and Brian Branch/Christian Izien at safety, with no Joseph. The official Week 10 injury report lists Joseph as Out (knee). The same pattern appears for Lucas Patrick (WAS, C, Out) and Malik Harrison (NYG, LB, Questionable): both are on the official injury report and absent from their club's published chart.

here.note: S rows list Clark, Branch, Izien only
Joseph, S, Knee, Full Participation, Out

findings.settle: None of the three sources is wrong on its face: a club may omit an injured player from its chart. The consequence is that a chart cannot be used alone to infer 'next man up' for an absent starter, so next-man-up rows are published only where the chart names a player behind him. Verified live today: the Commanders chart lists Colson Yankoff as the second tight end behind John Bates, and does not list Lucas Patrick at all.

findings.title: Depth charts carry no comparable date
findings.detail: Of 31 captured club charts, 3 publish a date on the page ('Nov. 10, 2026', '11/10/26', none) and the rest publish nothing machine-readable. A cross-club depth comparison therefore mixes snapshots of unknown age.
findings.settle: Record the fetch timestamp per club (already stored) and label the chart date as 'not published' rather than blank.

findings.title: The priced board cannot be reproduced from the committed extract: two sample counts disagree
findings.detail: The leaderboard reports 4,751 games in sample and 1,902 games not scored for want of a price, i.e. 6,653 candidate games. The committed data/s9cb/games.csv, restricted to 2006-2026 and to rows where the total line exists (a precondition for an over/under bet), holds 5,471 games. So the published totals and the committed file differ by more than a thousand games, and neither figure can be reconciled to the other from what is committed.
findings.settle: Either publish the collector's row filters and re-derive both counts, or publish the two numbers with their definitions side by side.

findings.title: The games excluded for missing prices are not evenly spread across seasons
findings.detail: Within 2006-2026, 243 games carry no spread price. They are concentrated: 2006 has 47 (18.4% of that season), 2008 has 71 (27.7%), 2026 has 109 (40.1%, because those games have not been played yet). Only 17 games in every other season are missing a price. The exclusion rule therefore removes mostly the oldest season in the window and the unfinished current season, which is a selection effect on any full-window result.

here.note: bets are scored only with an observed price

findings.settle: Report the per-season priced share next to every full-window ROI, or exclude the unfinished season explicitly.

findings.title: The leaderboard is ordered exactly as its caption says
findings.detail: Corrected during this review: an earlier draft of this page recorded a ranking-order defect. It was wrong. data/model/strategies.json is sorted by score_lower_ci_roi_pct descending (pipeline/build_all.py line 593), which matches the published sentence 'Ranked by the lower bound of the 95% ROI interval'. The gate counts in the rendered table merely happen to be non-monotonic. The claim was withdrawn before publication; it is recorded here so the withdrawal itself is auditable.
findings.settle: Nothing - the ordering is correct. Keep the sort-key unit test suggested in SG-03 so the caption and the code cannot drift apart.

findings.title: One club publishes its depth chart as an image, not as a table
findings.detail: Houston's depth-chart page carries the heading 'Unofficial Depth Chart' and then a single image. No position rows can be extracted without reading the picture, and this repository does not transcribe images into data. The club is therefore recorded as 'graphic': it does publish a chart, and this site still cannot state its depth order.
findings.settle: Either transcribe the image by hand with a reviewer's sign-off, or leave HOU blank and say why.
